blocks.text: Lots and land in Canyon Springs

items.t: Established house lots: detached houses under the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 (Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996), with strata product toward the Pinetree Way corridor. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character from the zones, as the City states it: minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2; the SSMUH unit counts turn on the 280 m² and 4,050 m² thresholds. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel: Not verified for any individual lot.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam's SSMUH framework expressly leaves lots not connected to municipal water or sewer OUTSIDE the SSMUH rules — the City's own servicing qualifier for house lots here — and Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste. Property-level septic or well status is not verified: confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before pricing in added units.

Watercourse / ravine character: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam — the sub-area name itself signals canyon / ravine terrain, and creek-edge lots carry permit and setback diligence.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area is not verified; no ALR parcel and no ALR percentage split is confirmed. ALR status is a property-specific check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Market context, labelled correctly: Coquitlam IS a SnapStats-covered community; SnapStats has NO land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: Canyon Springs sub-area detached inventory 10 / solds 1 (10%) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 21 / 5 (24%); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $625,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (community level only).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Canyon Springs

items.t: Canyon Springs is a small board sub-area in north-central Coquitlam, in the Pinetree Way / Town Centre side of the city. "Canyon Springs" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report; an official City of Coquitlam neighbourhood plan name for "Canyon Springs" was not confirmed — the City plans this part of Coquitlam through its City Centre / Town Centre planning and the Transit-Oriented Areas framework. Boundaries: NOT CONFIRMED — no City neighbourhood or community plan boundary for Canyon Springs is stated on a City page in the sources read: Not verified.
Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the south, North Coquitlam / City Centre (board naming) and Town Centre Park to the north-east, Burke Mountain beyond, and Coquitlam East to the east.

Transit: the nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas on Pinetree Way; Coquitlam Central Station, also on the Evergreen Extension, has West Coast Express service; per-route bus numbers serving Canyon Springs streets: Not verified. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.
Schools: SD43 (Coquitlam) catchments are address-based, in a three-tier system (elementary / middle / secondary).

Civic anchors: Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, and Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, serve Coquitlam; Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border and the nearest hospital for this area. Parks inside Canyon Springs by official name: Not verified pass; Town Centre Park is a City park name for north Coquitlam in City records.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Canyon Springs

items.t: Zoning — Coquitlam Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996: small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, with subdivision minimums of 650 m² / 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² / 12.5 m width (R-2).
Subdivision + servicing requirements — VERIFIED bylaw: Parcel-level servicing requirements are confirmed with the City for the specific lot.

Watercourse / flood diligence: a Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam, and Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses while s.523 covers riparian areas — check setbacks early on ravine and creek-edge lots, before pricing redevelopment value.

ALR rules (for completeness — sub-area ALR status not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

blocks.text: Good to know about Canyon Springs

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026 without changing the policy: the Interim OCP (Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026) superseded OCP No. 3479, and the City states it streamlined the former plan and introduced no new land-use policy except as provincial legislation required — so a Canyon Springs lot's plan position did not change with the number, but any document still citing No. 3479 as current is stale, and a fuller OCP update project is anticipated to begin in 2027.

The servicing bill has a name, a number — and owner-paid signage: subdivision servicing in Coquitlam runs under Bylaw No. 3558, 2003, a 2003 bylaw still being amended in July 2026, including solicitor-acceptable statutory rights-of-way for services and City-installed traffic-control and street-name signage at the owner's expense before approval. A split priced without a Bylaw 3558 servicing estimate is priced blind.

faq.q: Is Canyon Springs in Coquitlam or North Vancouver?
faq.a: "Canyon Springs" is a GVR sub-area name for this pocket of north-central Coquitlam. Verify the municipality on every Canyon Springs hit.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Canyon Springs?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering was verified. Land trades as built house lots and the Princess Crescent strata ground.

faq.q: Is a Canyon Springs lot serviced?
faq.a: The City's framework assumes municipal water and sewer for SSMUH eligibility and bills water, sewer/drainage and solid waste as City utilities — but parcel-level septic or well status is not verified, so confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before writing.

faq.q: What do the watercourse rules mean for a ravine-edge lot?
faq.a: A Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam, and Zoning Bylaw s.519 / s.523 set flood and riparian setbacks — run that check before pricing any redevelopment value on a creek-edge lot.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Pinetree Way address here?
faq.a: Pinetree Way Elementary, Summit Middle and Pinetree Secondary serve the sample address 1420 Pinetree Way. School District No. 43 (SD43) catchments are address-based in a three-tier system, and Pinetree Way Elementary itself is at 1420 Pinetree Way, so run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator rather than assuming every Canyon Springs street feeds the same three schools.

faq.q: Is Canyon Springs an official City neighbourhood?
faq.a: No. City documents group these streets with the City Centre and the Transit-Oriented Areas around the Evergreen Extension stations, which is the planning frame that actually governs rezoning and density here.

Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas, both Millennium Line (Evergreen Extension) stations on Pinetree Way, are the nearest stations named in City Transit-Oriented Areas documents. Coquitlam Central Station, also on the Evergreen Extension, adds West Coast Express service. Which station is walkable depends on the exact street, and no City source assigns a station to the sub-area as a whole.

faq.q: What runs through the park side of the area?
faq.a: Hoy Creek and its linear park trail system run beside Town Centre Park, with trailheads at Pinetree Way and Guildford Way shown on the City's Salmon Come Home event map. Creek-side lots are exactly where the 30-metre Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area and the Zoning Bylaw flood setbacks apply, so a creek address needs a permit check before any addition is designed.

faq.q: Can a Canyon Springs house lot add units?
faq.a: Yes under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes, where the zoning and municipal services allow.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve the area?
faq.a: Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) on Pinetree Way are the nearest stations named in City Transit-Oriented Areas documents, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express service.

faq.q: When were Coquitlam property taxes due in 2026?
faq.a: July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty after September 15, 2026, including unclaimed Home Owner Grants.
